note: Supplementary, source-linked presentation media. This file does not define spacecraft trajectories, rover coordinates, or new event times.

launch.alt: Delta II Heavy rocket carrying Opportunity lifts off from Cape Canaveral at night
launch.caption: The real Opportunity launch, 8 July 2003 UTC. The Earth-to-Mars line in the atlas is sampled from the archived MER1 SPICE cruise kernel.

landing.alt: Opportunity looks back at its empty landing platform and wheel tracks on Mars
landing.caption: The landing platform remained in Eagle Crater after the rover drove away.

water.alt: Close view of the Berry Bowl rock and its round hematite grains
water.caption: Round hematite-rich grains became one clue to ancient water.

endeavour.alt: Opportunity camera view after reaching Endeavour Crater's western rim
endeavour.caption: A rover-camera view from Spirit Point, on Endeavour's rim, August 2011.

last-signal.alt: Opportunity's final panoramic view from Perseverance Valley
last-signal.caption: The final panorama was acquired between 13 May and 10 June 2018.

legacy.alt: NASA annotated map of Opportunity's full traverse from Eagle Crater to Perseverance Valley
legacy.caption: NASA's published annotated traverse map, shown as an image rather than a reconstructed track.

route.description: The published image records Opportunity's overall traverse. This edition does not convert the drawn line into a coordinate-registered rover path or claim that the marker moves along it at the correct time.

highlights.title: A tiny crater with a big clue
highlights.summary: Opportunity landed inside Eagle Crater and found layered rocks and hematite-rich spheres that helped scientists infer past water.

image.alt: Berry Bowl rock with round grains photographed by Opportunity

highlights.title: A journey far beyond 90 sols
highlights.summary: The rover reached the western rim of Endeavour Crater on 9 August 2011, years after its planned three-month mission.

image.alt: Opportunity view from Spirit Point at Endeavour Crater

highlights.title: The last view
highlights.summary: Opportunity's final panorama looked across Perseverance Valley. Its last communication came on 10 June 2018 after a planet-wide dust storm reduced sunlight.

image.alt: Final Opportunity panorama from Perseverance Valley

launch.alt: Apollo 11 Saturn V rocket lifting off from Kennedy Space Center
launch.caption: Apollo 11 launched on 16 July 1969. This is a historical photograph, not a rendered trajectory.

highlights.title: The first human landing
highlights.summary: Apollo 11's Eagle lander reached Mare Tranquillitatis. Its descent stage and laser ranging retroreflector remained on the lunar surface.

landing.alt: First panoramic view by Viking 1 from the surface of Mars
landing.caption: Viking 1's camera looked over Chryse Planitia after landing in July 1976.

highlights.title: A first look from Mars
highlights.summary: Viking 1 touched down in Chryse Planitia on 20 July 1976 and returned images from the surface. Its biology experiments found no definitive evidence of life.
